    Four-parameter logistic dose-response curves (IC50 and EC50)

    Source: R/bio-assays.R
    bio_dose_response.Rd

    Fits the four-parameter logistic (4PL) model $$y = \mathrm{bottom} + \frac{\mathrm{top} - \mathrm{bottom}}{1 + (\mathrm{EC50} / x)^{\mathrm{hill}}}$$ to each group by Levenberg-Marquardt least squares, written in base R. bottom is always the lower asymptote and top the upper one. A negative Hill slope means the response falls with dose, so the midpoint is reported as an IC50; a positive slope gives an EC50. Zero doses are allowed and are treated as true zeros. Confidence intervals for the EC50 or IC50 are computed on the log scale.

    Usage

    bio_dose_response(
  .data,
  dose,
  response,
  .by = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  bottom = NULL,
  top = NULL,
  level = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame or tibble.

    dose, response

    <tidy-select> Columns holding dose (or concentration, on the original scale) and response.

    .by

    <tidy-select> Optional columns that define separate curves, such as compound or cell line.

    weights

    <tidy-select> Optional column of case weights.

    bottom, top

    Optional fixed values for the asymptotes, for example bottom = 0 for data normalised to percent of control.

    level

    Confidence level.

    Value

    A <bio_assay> with one row per curve: the .by columns, bottom, top, ec50, ec50_low, ec50_high, hill, type ("IC50" or "EC50"), sigma, nobs and converged. Use tidy() for full parameter tables and autoplot() to draw the curves.

    References

    Ritz, C., Baty, F., Streibig, J. C. and Gerhard, D. (2015). Dose-response analysis using R. PLOS ONE, 10, e0146021. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0146021

    Examples

    fit <- bio_dose_response(dose_response_sim, dose, response, .by = compound)
fit
#> # A bio_assay: dose_response: 3 x 11
#>   compound    bottom   top   ec50 ec50_low ec50_high  hill type  sigma  nobs
#>   <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl> <chr> <dbl> <int>
#> 1 activator_c   7.69  85.9 1.20     1.06      1.36    1.38 EC50   3.02    33
#> 2 inhibitor_a   4.02 102.  0.0490   0.0413    0.0581 -1.16 IC50   4.26    33
#> 3 inhibitor_b   9.31  98.6 2.34     2.07      2.65   -1.61 IC50   3.69    33
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: converged <lgl>
tidy(fit)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 8
#>    compound    term   estimate std.error statistic    p.value conf.low conf.high
#>    <chr>       <chr>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>

#>  2 activator_c top     85.9      1.21        71.2   4.05 e-34  83.5      88.4   
#>  3 activator_c ec50     1.20     0.0743      NA    NA           1.06      1.36  
#>  4 activator_c hill     1.38     0.104       13.2   8.70 e-14   1.16      1.59  
#>  5 inhibitor_a bottom   4.02     1.16         3.45  1.73 e- 3   1.64      6.40  
#>  6 inhibitor_a top    102.       2.15        47.4   5.05 e-29  97.6     106.    
#>  7 inhibitor_a ec50     0.0490   0.00408     NA    NA           0.0413    0.0581
#>  8 inhibitor_a hill    -1.16     0.0930     -12.5   3.53 e-13  -1.35     -0.970 
#>  9 inhibitor_b bottom   9.31     1.56         5.96  1.78 e- 6   6.11     12.5   
#> 10 inhibitor_b top     98.6      0.958      103.    1.000e-38  96.6     101.
